A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DIQ research, with the same title, method and experimental program. All 25 pages of each version, including figures, equations, tables and Appendices A–G, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original medical benchmark fine-tuning results, quadrant experiments, ablations, transfer experiments and clinical reasoning assessments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including the benchmark comparisons and selection analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and Algorithm 1 retain BiomedBERT difficulty estimation, gradient-dot-product influence, quadrant priorities and within-quadrant ranking. The new VLM framing introduces no visual component or changed training or inference procedure.

E1.justification: The same six training corpora, QA-only variants and nine downstream benchmarks are used. Appendix G retains the same coverage. Despite the VLM language added to the abstract and introduction, no image-input or multimodal evaluation is added.

E2.justification: Random, PPL, Similarity and LESS remain the selection baselines. The general-model, single-criterion and BERT-model comparisons also retain their comparator membership. The ClinicalBERT citation correction does not change the evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Both versions report the same LoRA settings, model sizes, retention ratios and answer-scoring procedure. The default 20 validation examples per downstream task, validation-size sweep, clinical assessment sample sizes and preference-learning setup are unchanged.

E4.justification: The quadrant pilot, single-score ablations, validation-size sensitivity, cross-scale and cross-family transfer, preference-learning analysis, clinical case study and score-distribution analyses are retained. Appendix reflow adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Table 1 continues to report averages over five repetitions, and the QA experiment still specifies five-run averages. There are no changes to seed information, uncertainty reporting or significance-testing practices.

E6.justification: All 13 tables retain their numerical results, and plotted results and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains Huatuo DIQ AvgA values of 42.78 and 44.04 at 1% and 10% retention; Table 4 retains 56.52 for 1% DIQ plus DPO.

T1.justification: Equation 1 replaces the empirical loss sum with an empirical expectation, preserving the minimizer. Equation 6 makes the existing summation domain explicit. These are equivalent notation changes; the influence derivation, assumptions and appendix FLOPs formulas remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract substantially broadens the claimed application from medical LLM fine-tuning to efficient medical reasoning for VLMs, attributing the 1% data-efficiency result to VLM backbones. The first contribution now claims robust language foundations for medical VLMs, although the supporting experiments remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The introduction adds an applicability rationale connecting language backbones to multimodal medicine and visually derived clinical information. Detailed interpretations of the experiments, cross-family transfer caveats and the limitation concerning models of at least 70B parameters remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability statement and repository link in the abstract, absent from v2. Implementation settings, hardware, annotation prompts and influence-rater training details are otherwise retained. The PDFs alone do not verify the repository contents.

R1.justification: v3 adds Koh and Liang's influence-function paper and cites the existing TracIn reference in the introduction. It replaces the unrelated diabetes reinforcement-learning reference attached to ClinicalBERT with Huang and colleagues' ClinicalBERT paper. The related-work survey otherwise remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits concentrate on the abstract and opening motivation, with smaller method wording changes and a renamed Section 3.3. v3 also adds appendix contents and an acknowledgement, and updates affiliation numbering and contact information. The main section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Table 2 becomes narrower, abbreviating Safety Check and Evidence Citation as SC and EC and explaining them in its caption. Figure 1's caption is refined, Table 5 moves from PDF page 12 to 13, and appendix floats reflow. Existing graphics are retained and printed page numbers disappear.

improvement.justification: The code-access statement, corrected ClinicalBERT citation and appendix contents provide modest documentation benefits. However, v3's abstract now asserts VLM benefits while Sections 4–5 and Appendix G retain the same LLM experiments, without reported VLM integration or multimodal evaluation. This weakens the alignment between headline claims and demonstrated evidence, producing a limited overall decline despite the documentation improvements.
